Three months ago, he saw a light on the horizon at night — not a star, not a ship's lamp, but a steady green glow beneath the water's surface, moving slowly north. He has seen it every night since, and it is closer. It moves against the current and the wind, as if it has its own direction. It is now close enough that he can see it is not a single light but a formation — a line of lights, evenly spaced, moving in formation like a convoy. He has not reported it because he does not know what it is, and he is afraid that if he reports it, the response will be a war fleet — and if the lights are refugees from somewhere farther south, a war fleet would be a catastrophe. He is also afraid that if the lights are not refugees, a war fleet would be too late.

payload.summary: A southern watchtower scout who has been tracking a formation of underwater lights moving north toward the Archipelago. They are getting closer every night, and he has not told anyone.
payload.appearance: A young, lean man with a scout's trained eyes and a watcher's patience. He spends most of his time in the watchtower and has the sun-weathered look of someone who is always outdoors.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, wind-tossed
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a scout's watchtower — he is almost always in it, a spyglass worn on a cord around the neck, a logbook of observations he keeps private, dark circles under the eyes from sleepless nights of watching the southern horizon

desires: To identify the underwater lights before they reach the Archipelago — and to determine if they are a threat or people in need
To find the courage to report what he has seen — to trust that the response will be wise rather than violent
fears_or_limits: That the lights are an approaching threat and his hesitation to report has cost the Archipelago its chance to prepare
That the lights are a convoy of refugees fleeing something worse than the rising seas — and that they will be met with fear instead of welcome

entries.name: Vili Deep-Lung
entries.gm_notes: Vili is a pearl diver, one of the few men in the profession, and he is known for his deep dives — deeper than anyone else in the Archipelago. He can reach depths that would kill most divers, and he has never suffered the sickness that affects divers who surface too fast. His secret is that he should not be able to do this. He has gills. Not visible ones — slits along his ribcage that open when he is submerged and close when he is in air. They are hidden beneath his arms and are invisible unless he raises his arms above his head in water. He has had them since birth and has never shown anyone, not even his wife. He has been diving deeper and deeper, not for pearls but to explore the sea floor, and he has seen things that no one else can reach — including, recently, structures beneath the Archipelago that are too regular to be natural. He has seen what looks like a foundation — a vast, flat stone surface beneath the islands, as if the Archipelago was built on something. He is afraid that his gills are not a mutation but a heritage — that someone in his bloodline was not entirely human, and that what lives beneath the islands is where he came from.

payload.summary: A pearl diver with hidden gills who can reach depths no one else survives. He has seen structures beneath the Archipelago — a vast stone foundation, as if the islands were built on something.
payload.appearance: A lean, deep-chested man with a diver's build and an ease in the water that is unsettling to watch. He moves through the sea as if it is his natural element, which, secretly, it is.

visual_identity.hair: black, cropped short, water-slicked
visual_identity.eyes: grey-green — the color of deep water
visual_identity.distinctive_features: hidden gill slits along both sides of the ribcage — invisible unless arms are raised in water, an unnatural ease in the water that other divers find remarkable but unsettling, a diver's barotrauma scarring on both earlobes that has healed despite the depth he reaches

desires: To dive to the foundation he has seen and determine what the islands were built on — and by whom
To find out if his gills are a gift from something beneath the sea — and whether that something is still alive
fears_or_limits: That his gills mark him as descended from whatever built the foundation — and that the rising seas are calling him home to something that is not human
That someone will see his gills and he will be driven from the community as something other than human

entries.name: Tama-iti Little-Wave
entries.gm_notes: Tama-iti is an eight-year-old boy, the son of a refugee family living on Lani Atoll. He is bright, curious, and always underfoot, and the adults tolerate him with the affectionate exasperation reserved for children who are everywhere at once. His secret is that he has a friend no one else can see. The friend is tall, made of water, and lives in the lagoon. It appeared to him the day he arrived on the atoll, and it has been with him every day since. It does not speak — it shows him things by changing shape. It showed him a picture of a canoe, and the next day a canoe arrived with refugees. It showed him a picture of a storm, and a storm came. It showed him a picture of an island with water rising around it, and he does not know which island it is or when it will happen. He told his mother about the friend once, and she told him it was a dream from the journey. He has not mentioned it again, but he goes to the lagoon every day to see what his friend will show him next. He is eight, and he does not know that what he is describing is a spirit, and he does not know that it is showing him the future, and he does not know that the next picture it shows him might be of Lani Atoll.

payload.summary: An eight-year-old refugee boy who has a water-spirit friend in the lagoon that shows him visions of the future. He does not know what it is — only that it is his friend.
payload.appearance: A small, bright-eyed boy who is always near the water and always looking at it. He wears refugee-donated clothing that is too large for him, and he has the restless energy of a child who has lost his home and is looking for a new one.

visual_identity.hair: black, short, untidy
visual_identity.eyes: dark brown, very bright and curious
visual_identity.distinctive_features: donated clothing that is always too large, a constant proximity to the water's edge — he is always near the lagoon, a habit of watching the water and smiling at things no one else can see, sand always on his feet

desires: To see what his water-friend will show him next — and to understand the pictures it makes
To find someone who can see his friend too — so he can prove it is real and not a dream
fears_or_limits: That his friend will show him a picture of his new home — Lani Atoll — with water rising around it
That his friend will disappear the way his old home did — suddenly and without explanation

entries.name: Rotama Quiet-Weave
entries.gm_notes: Rotama is a sail maker's apprentice who works under Leilani Wave-Singer. She is quiet, diligent, and learns fast. She is fifteen and one of the youngest apprentices in the craft. Her secret is that she can see the wind. Not feel it — see it. The air moves in visible currents to her eyes, colored faintly by temperature and moisture. She has always seen this and assumed everyone did. When she realized that others could not, she said nothing, because the ability lets her trim sails more precisely than any sailor and she did not want to be treated as a freak. But she has been watching the wind patterns change over the past year, and what she sees terrifies her. The wind is not just changing direction — it is being displaced. Something is pushing the air aside, something very large and very high that she can see only as a disturbance in the wind patterns — a shape that is not visible but that the wind flows around. It is north of the Archipelago, high in the sky, and it is getting larger. She has not told Leilani because she does not know how to describe what she sees without sounding insane.

payload.summary: A fifteen-year-old sail maker's apprentice who can see the wind — and who has been watching something invisible displace the air north of the Archipelago. It is large, high, and growing.
payload.appearance: A small, quiet girl with a sail maker's stained hands and a tendency to watch the sky when others watch the sea. She is diligent and eager to please and terrified of something she cannot explain.

visual_identity.hair: black, long, tied back for work
visual_identity.eyes: pale blue — unusually light, almost colorless, which she hides by looking down
visual_identity.distinctive_features: sail-cloth dye staining on both hands, pale blue eyes that are unusual for the Archipelago — she avoids eye contact to hide them, a habit of watching the sky rather than the sea, a tension in her shoulders that has grown over the past year

desires: To find someone who can see what she sees in the wind — or someone who can help her understand the invisible shape displacing the air
To tell Leilani what she sees and be believed — to share the burden of a sight no one else has
fears_or_limits: That the invisible shape in the sky is connected to the rising seas — and that no one will believe a fifteen-year-old apprentice who says she can see the wind
That the shape is growing because it is descending — and that when it reaches the water, it will be too late to do anything

entries.name: Keola Song-Keeper
entries.gm_notes: Keola is a song-keeper, one of the few who maintains the route-songs — the chants that wayfinders use to memorize the star paths and current patterns between islands. She is precise, dedicated, and has a voice like a bell. Her secret is that she has been altering the route-songs. Not the old ones — the ones she teaches to new wayfinders. She has been adding verses that include instructions for routes that do not exist yet — routes to islands that are farther north and higher, routes that follow the new reef channels that Moana Reef-Walker has been mapping. Keola does not know Moana, and Moana does not know Keola. But Keola has been having dreams of new routes, and she has been encoding them into the songs, so that when the time comes, there will be wayfinders who know the way to safety without knowing how they know. She is afraid she is inventing routes that do not exist and leading wayfinders to their deaths. She is also afraid that the routes are real and that the dreams are showing her a future in which the current islands are gone and the new routes are the only way to survive.

payload.summary: A song-keeper who has been secretly encoding new route-songs for routes that do not exist yet — routes to higher, northern islands she has seen in dreams. She does not know if she is prophesying or inventing.
payload.appearance: A precise, clear-voiced woman with a song-keeper's trained memory and a scholar's careful habits. She carries tapa-books of notation and rehearses constantly, her lips moving in silent chant.

visual_identity.hair: black, worn in a song-keeper's braided style with shell pins
visual_identity.distinctive_features: tapa-books of chant notation carried under the arm, shell pins in the hair marking her as a song-keeper, a habit of silent lip movement — she is always rehearsing, a tension between precision and uncertainty that has grown over the past year

desires: To determine whether the dream-routes are real — to find a wayfinder willing to sail a route that exists only in a song
To prepare the Archipelago for a future in which the current islands are gone — without causing panic in the present
fears_or_limits: That the dream-routes are inventions and she has been teaching wayfinders to sail into nothing
That the routes are real but lead somewhere that is not safe — that the dreams are not guidance but a lure

_help: Bonds between people. Keep the shared and private halves separate:
`public_status` is what anyone can observe; `bond` is your assessment and
stays GM-side.
`disposition` is a number from -100 to 100. It is stored today and does
not drift on its own yet (Phase 2, W2.3).

entries.name: Sir Aldrich and the Dragon Order

payload.public_status: A respected senior knight, loyal to the order, though quiet at council meetings.
payload.bond: Aldrich is losing faith in the order's ability to resolve its own crisis. He stays because leaving would confirm the traditionalists' fears, but he is privately sympathetic to the reformers. His silence at council meetings is not loyalty — it is indecision.

entries.name: Cao Shen and General Lu Fang

payload.public_status: Cao Shen trusts Lu Fang with military command. Lu Fang is publicly loyal and has never failed an order.
payload.bond: Cao Shen suspects Lu Fang's loyalty is to the idea of a unified Sangguo, not specifically to Cao Shen. If Cao Shen dies before reunification, Lu Fang may pursue it himself — in his own way, which may be less careful.

payload.public_status: The king's two eldest children, publicly civil, privately competing for the succession. The court watches them and bets quietly.
payload.bond: Elara underestimates Roderick's cunning — she thinks he is a blunt soldier, but he has been feeding her false intelligence through a double agent. Roderick does not know about Elara's dragonbone research, which is the one card she has that he cannot counter. They are siblings and they are enemies, and neither of them has decided which matters more.

payload.public_status: Two jarls who disagree about the frost giant threat. Sigrid wants action; Erik wants restraint. The Althing watches them and waits.
payload.bond: Sigrid thinks Erik is naive about the giants. Erik thinks Sigrid is using the giants to consolidate power. Both are partly right, which makes the rivalry productive and dangerous. If the abandoned village goes public, Erik's position collapses and Sigrid wins — which is why Sigrid has been sitting on the information.

entries.name: Malik Idris and Zuhayr the Patient

payload.public_status: Malik is the heir to the Idris family's oldest djinn contract. Zuhayr is the djinn bound by it. The contract's terms are family knowledge but not public.
payload.bond: Zuhayr genuinely wants to help Malik renegotiate — a willing partner is more useful than a bound servant. But the contract's deadline is binding on both of them, and neither can extend it alone. Zuhayr is the most dangerous kind of ally: one who is on Malik's side but constrained by law from giving him more time. Their relationship is warm in a way that makes the debt more painful, not less.

payload.public_status: A young wayfinder and the chief of Lani Atoll. They maintain professional distance in public, as a chief should not favor one wayfinder over others.
payload.bond: They are mother and son, and both know it, and neither says it in public. Kai respects his mother's governance and does not want to compromise it. Lani is proud of her son and frightened for him — he is sailing toward something neither of them understands. Their private relationship is warm; their public one is careful.

payload.public_status: Nara is training Tari in the shamanic traditions. Tari is young and talented. A normal master-apprentice relationship.
payload.bond: Nara knows Tari is gifted but does not realize how much Tari is hearing that Nara is not. Tari is afraid of being dismissed as too young, and afraid of being taken seriously. They trust each other but are both keeping secrets — Nara about the river spirit's warning, Tari about the multiple spirits speaking to her. The secrets are about the same thing, and neither knows the other already knows.

payload.public_status: No public relationship. A daimyo and a wild kitsune would not be seen together.
payload.bond: Takeda thinks he is using Tamamo to create yokai incidents that prove the shrine network's weakness. Tamamo is using Takeda to weaken the wards she hates. Neither trusts the other. Both believe they are the one in control. They are both wrong.

entries.name: Garrick the Wolf and Maggie Pippin

payload.association: bandit and innkeeper, uneasy mutual tolerance
payload.public_status: Maggie's inn is on the Greywood road, which Garrick controls. He does not rob her. She does not report him. A practical arrangement.
payload.bond: Maggie feeds Garrick information about travelers in exchange for him keeping the road safe from other bandits. She does not approve of his methods but recognizes that his presence is better than the alternative. Garrick is protective of the inn in a way he would not admit — Maggie reminds him of his mother, who ran a similar inn before the war.

entries.name: Skald Ravn and Grimvard the Patient

payload.public_status: A frost giant is sitting outside Skaldvik because the skald's poem got the giants' history wrong. Ravn thinks it is funny. Everyone else is nervous.
payload.bond: Grimvard respects Ravn's skill as a poet — the poem is beautiful, it is just inaccurate. Ravn is beginning to realize that the giant is not threatening but correcting, and that the corrections contain information about the deep mountains that no human scout has brought back. They are on the verge of a conversation that could change Hrafnland's understanding of the frost giants entirely.

entries.name: Shrine maiden and her mentor keeper

payload.public_status: Yuki serves under Miko Sora at the shrine, learning the rites and purification ceremonies as a junior maiden.
payload.bond: Sora sees in Yuki a spiritual sensitivity she herself lacked at that age, and pushes her harder than she lets on — terrified the gifts will corrupt the girl if left undisciplined. Yuki sometimes resents the severity but would never say so, believing Sora is preparing her for something Sora cannot speak of yet.

payload.public_status: Daimyo Takeda is a loyal provincial lord to Shogun Ashikara, governing his lands in the shogun's name.
payload.bond: Takeda has grown privately disillusioned with the shogun's indecision and courtly excess, believing the realm needs a steadier hand. He obeys outwardly but has begun quietly consolidating retainers, walking a razor's edge between loyal vassal and threat.

entries.name: Tea house owner and sake brewer, drinking companions

payload.public_status: The tea house owner and the sake brewer are known to be old friends who share drinks after hours and refer customers to each other.
payload.bond: Their friendship predates both their businesses — they survived a famine together as young women, rationing what little they had. Neither married, and the town quietly assumes they are simply set in their ways; in truth they are the closest thing to family either has.

payload.public_status: Jiro, a retired ronin, occasionally trains with the tengu swordmaster Soji, though most assume the old bodyguard's days of fighting are past.
payload.bond: Soji sees in Jiro a swordsman who stopped growing before he reached his potential — a man who served others so long he forgot his own blade. The tengu is trying to reawaken that instinct before Jiro's body fails him entirely. Jiro suspects Soji is preparing him for one final, necessary cut.

entries.name: Thief and gambling den owner, covert arrangement

payload.public_status: Kuro is known to frequent Rui's gambling den, where the thief is said to lose more than he wins.
payload.bond: The losses are theater. Rui fences what Kuro steals and feeds him targets among the den's wealthy, careless patrons. Each believes they are the one truly in control of the arrangement, and neither has noticed how easily it could collapse if either's price were met.

entries.name: Female samurai and palace guard captain

payload.public_status: The onna-bugeisha of the Takeda clan and the shogunate's guard captain are regarded as professional peers who cross paths at official functions.
payload.bond: They have been meeting in private for over a year, each serving masters whose political interests are slowly diverging. The romance is genuine but laced with dread — each knows the day may come when their loyalties demand they stand on opposite sides of a courtyard, weapons drawn.

payload.public_status: Machi the merchant is a known patron of Kohana's tea house entertainments, nothing more.
payload.bond: Kohana hears what powerful men say when they believe they are only entertaining a courtesan, and Machi moves goods and favors based on what she tells him. Neither is sentimental about it — it is commerce — but both understand that exposure would ruin them equally.

entries.name: The two princes of the Ashikara shogunate

payload.public_status: The elder and younger princes of the Ashikara line are presented at court as a united front, each supporting the other's roles.
payload.bond: Renjiro, the elder, believes the succession should be his by right of birth but lacks the younger Haru's easy charm with the court. Haru does not want the throne but fears what his brother would do with it. They smile in public and measure each other in private, each waiting for the other to move first.

payload.public_status: The two fox spirits are occasionally seen near the shrine grounds together, though most folk cannot tell them apart and assume them the same creature.
payload.bond: Katsura is Tamamo's younger kinspirit, bound to the shrine by pact where Tamamo refused all such ties. They argue in the fox-tongue about freedom and duty — Katsura believing Tamamo foolish for spurning the shrine's protection, Tamamo believing Katsure has traded her wild soul for safety. They love each other fiercely and neither will admit it.

payload.public_status: The archivist and the tutor are known to debate historical interpretation at length, sometimes heatedly, in the library reading room.
payload.bond: Their rivalry began over a single contested manuscript — each read the same faded text and reached opposite conclusions about a suppressed rebellion. What started as scholarly pride has become genuine intellectual respect neither will voice, because conceding any point feels like conceding the war.

entries.name: Double agent servant and the daimyo

payload.public_status: Tomi is a household servant within the Takeda clan's service, unremarkable and overlooked.
payload.bond: Tomi reports to Daimyo Takeda on the shogunate's interior movements — a spy placed so low in the household that no one thinks to watch her. Takeda treats her with a quiet courtesy he shows no other servant, which is the only thing preventing her from being made. She has begun to wonder what happens to her the day she is no longer useful.

payload.public_status: The herbalist and the florist work adjacent trades and are often seen sharing cuttings and market gossip.
payload.bond: They have an unspoken pact: Rin grows the beauty, Nana grows the medicine, and between them they tend a private garden plot no one else knows of, where they've planted seeds from their grandmothers' generation — living memory of a time before the shogunate's roads reached this far.

entries.name: King and baroness mediator, political confidantes

payload.public_status: Baroness Gwendolyn Fairhold is known as a political mediator occasionally summoned to the king's court to settle noble disputes.
payload.bond: Aldran trusts Gwendolyn more than his own council because she has no faction — her power comes from being acceptable to all houses. He uses her as a backchannel to test policies and sound out potential betrayals before they ripen. She accepts because the arrangement gives her leverage no title could, though she wonders how long she can stay everyone's neutral party.

payload.public_status: Lyria Ironheart and Regor Blackhammer are the two foremost smiths in the town, and their competition for commissions is well known.
payload.bond: They were once apprenticed to the same master and loved each other as siblings before pride and a disputed inheritance of the forge divided them. Each secretly believes the other was the more talented and resents being forced to prove otherwise every single day.

payload.public_status: Squire Maren Stormwing serves under the retired knight Aldric Stonehand, training in arms at the Dragon Order's training yard.
payload.bond: Aldric sees in Maren the same hunger that got his own first squire killed, and he is harder on the young squire than anyone realizes — not out of cruelty, but out of terror. Maren mistakes the severity for doubt and pushes harder to prove worthy, which is exactly what Aldric fears.

payload.public_status: Dawnspear and Drakesworn are the two most prominent active dragon-bonded knights of the Order, often compared in tavern talk.
payload.bond: Their dragons are siblings of the same clutch, and the beasts' own competitive bond bleeds upward into the riders. What looks like knightly rivalry is partly a domestic argument conducted through ten tons of scales and fire — each rider half-convinced the other's dragon is the favorite of the bloodline.

payload.public_status: Mira Greenbottle and Sybil Ashroot are both herbalists serving overlapping quarters, and locals debate whose tinctures are superior.
payload.bond: Sybil, the midwife, handles the births and the deaths; Mira handles everything in between. The professional boundary was once a courtesy and is now a cold war — each suspects the other of poaching patients, and neither will admit how much they rely on the other's expertise when a case exceeds their own.

entries.name: Tavern keeper and innkeeper, competing hosts

payload.public_status: The tavern keeper and the innkeeper are neighboring establishments and apparent competitors for travelers' coin.
payload.bond: The competition is a long-running performance they both maintain to keep prices credible. In truth they share staff, split bulk supplies, and send overflow custom to each other. Their partnership is the reason the riverfront district hasn't been bought out by outside interests — and neither wants that known.

entries.name: Baker and mead brewer, market companions

payload.public_status: The baker and the mead brewer are known to share a market stall and trade goods — bread for mead — on festival days.
payload.bond: Their friendship is the warm, uncomplicated kind that comes of having survived the same lean winter and vowed never to let the other go hungry again. Margaret keeps Becka fed when the brewing season is lean; Becka keeps Margaret's spirits up when the ovens feel like a prison. Neither has ever needed to say any of this aloud.

payload.public_status: The mercenary captain and the bounty hunter are known to cross paths professionally and are said to dislike each other.
payload.bond: Years ago, Sable was hired to bring in a deserter who had joined Marcus's company. Marcus refused to give him up, and Sable took him anyway — killing two of Marcus's men in the process. The deserter hanged. Marcus has neither forgiven nor forgotten, and Sable knows it, and watches her own back whenever his company is in town.

entries.name: Two elven elders of the forests

payload.public_status: Lindrel of the Greenhall and Rowan Silverbranch are both elven elders of the region's forests, and are said to consult on woodland matters.
payload.bond: They are old — old even for elves — and were friends before the human kingdom of Valdris existed. They meet rarely now, having retreated to separate groves, but when they do it is as if no time has passed. Their chief unspoken grief is that they will likely outlive every human they currently know, together.

entries.name: Orphanage matron and the street child she can't catch

payload.public_status: The orphanage matron is known to chase the street child Daisy away from her kitchen door, and Daisy is known to steal from her anyway.
payload.bond: Hilda leaves food where Daisy can find it and pretends not to notice the theft; Daisy steals less than she could and pretends not to need the help. Each is too proud to name what they have become to each other, but Hilda has already made up a bed with Daisy's name on it, and Daisy knows which window is unlocked.

entries.name: Priest and monk-scribe, faith and ink

payload.public_status: The priest and the monk-scribe are known to collaborate on copying holy texts and preserving old records.
payload.bond: Their friendship is built on a shared private doubt: both have begun to suspect that the oldest records say something different from what the current church teaches. They copy the texts faithfully and say nothing, but their silences over the writing desk have grown longer and more weighted with each shared page.

payload.public_status: The forester and the shepherd work the same high pastures and are often seen walking the ridge trails together.
payload.bond: They are the only two who regularly go as deep into the hinterwoods as they do, and they have an unspoken agreement to watch each other's back on the trail. Neither is a talker, which is precisely why they get along — a friendship maintained in comfortable silence over miles of forest and field.

payload.public_status: The warlord of Jin and the warlord of Chu are the principal rivals of the Sangguo conflict, and their enmity is the stuff of popular legend.
payload.bond: They were once sworn brothers under the same banner before ambition split them. Each remembers the exact betrayal — though they disagree on who struck first — and neither will rest while the other holds land. The personal hatred has long outlasted any strategic rationale for the war between their states.

payload.public_status: Strategist Mei Lin of Jin and the master strategist Cao Mengshi of Wei are both known as brilliant advisors, and their names are often compared in court.
payload.bond: Mei Lin admires Cao Mengshi's work and privately models herself on it; Cao Mengshi regards her as the only living thinker who might one day surpass him, and is unsure whether to nurture or neutralize that. They have never met, but their writings circulate and each has begun writing with the other in mind as audience.

entries.name: Two information brokers of the trade routes

payload.public_status: Zhou Ba the merchant and Su Wanqing the tea merchant are both known to trade in information as much as goods, and their networks overlap.
payload.bond: Each knows the other is the only broker in Sangguo whose network rivals their own, and they have settled into an uneasy territorial agreement — Zhou handles the military and warlord traffic, Su Wanqing handles the Academy and scholar traffic. Both are waiting for the other to break the truce first.

payload.public_status: Hua Suxin and Cui Zhenbo are both physicians attached to the Jin court, and their competing diagnoses are a subject of court gossip.
payload.bond: Cui Zhenbo knows a secret about a poisoning that Hua Suxin has been chasing for years — he treated the victim and altered the records to protect the poisoner, who is powerful. Hua Suxin suspects the records were tampered with but not by whom. Every professional interaction between them is a quiet interrogation.

entries.name: General's wife spymaster and court socialite double agent

payload.public_status: The general's wife of Chu and the court socialite are known to move in the same Chu court circles and attend the same salons.
payload.bond: Yan Qiulin runs Chu's spy network from behind her husband's name, and Pan Yaqing is her most placed asset — a double agent ostensibly serving Jin while reporting everything back to Qiulin. The arrangement is fragile: Yaqing has begun to wonder whether Qiulin would sacrifice her to protect a bigger operation, and Qiulin has begun to wonder the same thing in reverse.

entries.name: Court musician and court dancer of Chu

payload.public_status: The court musician and the court dancer often perform together at Chu state functions and are regarded as artistic collaborators.
payload.bond: Both are quietly embedded: Zhiyao reports to Jin, Xueling is an assassin-in-waiting biding her moment. Neither knows the other's true purpose, but each has noticed the other's careful wrong notes — the small discrepancies that only someone living a double life would recognize. They are circling each other, not yet sure whether they are allies or targets.

entries.name: Martial arts teacher and senior archivist at the Academy

payload.public_status: The martial arts teacher and the senior archivist are both long-serving members of the Great Academy and are known to share tea and conversation.
payload.bond: Their friendship rests on a shared pacifist conviction that neither of their colleagues fully shares — Haichen teaches martial arts to prevent violence, and Shuyi preserves forbidden history so it is not repeated. They are each other's conscience, the one person who understands why they do what they do.

entries.name: Treasury official and the coerced Jin spy

payload.public_status: The Chu treasury official and a palace servant are known to have no particular relationship beyond passing in the halls.
payload.bond: Shen Wuguang secretly funds an orphanage and discovered that Ai Gulan, the Wei palace servant, was coerced into spying for Jin. Rather than expose her, he chose to protect her — feeding her harmless information to send back, shielding both her and the orphans. She does not know why he helps; he does not know whether trusting her will get him killed.

payload.public_status: Two Academy scholars known for their reformist leanings and their collaboration on questions of historical record.
payload.bond: Wenzhao writes the reformist arguments; Lianshu provides the documentary evidence that supports them by investigating tampering in the archives. They believe they are uncovering the truth together. What Lianshu has not yet told Wenzhao is that the trail of tampering leads toward a faction that would kill them both if it knew what they had found.

entries.name: Warlord's hidden prodigy son and the child chi-prodigy

payload.public_status: The warlord's youngest son and the child prodigy are not publicly known to have any connection.
payload.bond: Both are chi-prodigies, and both are objects of a three-way search by Jin, Wei, and Chu agents who want to control or destroy such power. They have been secretly introduced by intermediaries and recognized in each other the same frightening gift. The bond is that of endangered kin — not blood, but the family of those who share a dangerous difference.

entries.name: Palace guard captain and the fugitive whistleblower

payload.public_status: The Jin palace guard captain is tasked with internal security; the fugitive chi-cultivator is wanted by the Jin state. No public connection is known.
payload.bond: Chenyu is the hidden investigator the warlord uses to find internal threats, and Mengxue is the whistleblower who fled after exposing a chi-warfare program. Chenyu has been ordered to find her; Mengxue knows he is coming and has prepared for it. What neither expects is that the evidence she carries implicates the very warlord Chenyu serves.

entries.name: Restaurateur and rice farmer, deserter sanctuary

payload.public_status: A veteran restaurateur of Jin and a rice farmer have no publicly known relationship.
payload.bond: Together they run a hidden sanctuary for army deserters — Yuanshan provides shelter and work in his kitchens, Qiaomu provides food and cover stories from the farm. Both could be executed for it. The bond is one of quiet conscience: neither can stomach the war anymore, and this is the only way they have found to say so.

payload.public_status: Shaman Nara and Yara Moonflower are both regarded as powerful shamans of the Verdania peoples, and their differing counsel is sometimes sought in tandem.
payload.bond: They were apprentices to the same master and inherited opposing halves of the spirit-pact tradition — Nara speaks with the animal spirits, Yara with the plant and ancestor spirits. Each believes the other's pact is incomplete without their own, and each is too proud to propose reuniting what their master deliberately split.

payload.public_status: Tari, apprentice to Shaman Nara, and Iuri, a shaman-in-training of the Moonflower line, are known to spend time together at tribal gatherings.
payload.bond: They are the two youngest bearers of the old pacts, and the loneliness of that responsibility has made them fast friends. They share what their mentors will not yet teach them and cover for each other when the rituals go wrong — which is often. The friendship is the only place either can admit how frightened they are of what they are becoming.

entries.name: Two hunters of the deep forest

payload.public_status: Kaa the Jaguar-kin and Miri Jaguar-Shadow are both renowned hunters and are known to coordinate on difficult tracking.
payload.bond: They are bonded not by blood but by the hunt — they have saved each other's lives in the deep canopy more times than either counts. Kaa, the jaguar-kin, moves where Miri cannot; Miri reads sign that Kaa's senses miss. The unspoken rule is that if one is killed in the forest, the other does not come back alone.

entries.name: Chief of Iara and the chief's wife

payload.public_status: Chief Oron and Sol Many-Seasons are husband and wife and jointly lead the Iara community, she as elder council member, he as chief.
payload.bond: Their partnership is the marriage of two complementary powers — his is the voice that speaks for the people in war, hers is the memory that speaks for them in council. They disagree often and loudly, to the alarm of outsiders, but it is the disagreement of two people who have already agreed on the one thing that matters: the people come first.

entries.name: Two river pilots, masters of the current

payload.public_status: Corrente Watersong and Bahri Swift-Current are both master river pilots and are known to compete for the most challenging navigation contracts.
payload.bond: Each believes they alone know the true pulse of the great river, and each is half right — Corrente reads the deep current, Bahri reads the surface and the weather. Their rivalry is the reason no single pilot holds a monopoly on the waterways, which suits the tribes fine, even if it exhausts the two of them.

entries.name: Master feather worker and headdress restorer

payload.public_status: Tito Feather-Bound works under Quilla Featherhand, learning the restoration of old headdresses and ceremonial featherwork.
payload.bond: Quilla is passing on a craft that nearly died with her generation, and Tito is the only apprentice with the patience for it. What Tito does not yet know is that Quilla is also passing on the meanings encoded in the patterns — a ceremonial language the tribe believes is lost. She is deciding, lesson by lesson, whether he is ready to be told.

payload.public_status: Flor do Mato and Temno Root-Biter are both herbalists of the Verdania peoples, and locals consult each for different needs.
payload.bond: Flor heals; Temno deals in poisons and antidotes. The professional boundary is clear, but the personal one is not — each suspects the other knows formulations they have not shared, and each has been quietly trying to learn the other's secrets for years without ever directly asking.

entries.name: Master drummer and the dream-wine fermenter

payload.public_status: The master drummer and the dream-wine maker are known to collaborate on tribal rituals — his drums set the rhythm, her dream-wine opens the vision.
payload.bond: Their friendship is the partnership of two crafts that only work together — the drum-trance needs the wine to deepen it, and the wine needs the drum to direct it. They have learned each other's timing so precisely that a ceremony between them is almost wordless, and the community has noticed that their rituals are the only ones that reliably reach the spirit world.

payload.public_status: The ceremonial trance-dancer and the wind-flute player are known to perform together at tribal rituals, his melody driving her movement.
payload.bond: They are each other's only peer in spirit-work through performance — Estrela channels the trance and Vento's flute is what calls her into and back out of it. The trust required is absolute: if he stops playing at the wrong moment, she may not return. Neither has ever said how frightening that is, because saying it would make it more real.

entries.name: Sail maker apprentice and the master sail maker

payload.public_status: Alvilda Longthread is apprenticed to Thora Linenhand, the master sail maker of Skaldvik, learning the craft at the waterfront loft.
payload.bond: Thora is teaching her apprentice faster than is customary because her hands are stiffening and she has not told anyone how fast. Alvilda has noticed the master wincing over the stitching and suspects the truth but will not name it, afraid that saying it aloud will make Thora stop teaching out of pride. Each is trying to prepare the other for a transition neither will mention.

entries.name: Two glassblowers, accidental magician and reluctant weaponsmith

payload.public_status: Dunya al-Zujaj and Nabil al-Zujaj are both glassblowers of the same quarter and share a workshop name, and are assumed to be kin.
payload.bond: They are siblings who inherited the same furnace, and each has stumbled into a dangerous secret the other does not know — Dunya's glass accidentally channels djinn-fire, and Nabil has been coerced into shaping glass weapons for a binding family. Each is protecting the other by hiding what they do after hours, and the day their two secrets collide in the same furnace may burn the workshop to the ground.

entries.name: Inter-tribal trader and salt-trade journey leader

payload.public_status: Marcela Good-Trade and Suri Salt-Scales are both women who lead trade journeys between the tribes and are known to compete for routes and contracts.
payload.bond: Their rivalry is professional but personal — they were once partners on the same trade circuit before a dispute over a cheated village split them. Each now runs a parallel route, and each quietly ensures her prices in that village stay just below the other's, a war of conscience neither will win and neither will stop.

entries.name: Temple ruin guardian and genealogy keeper

payload.public_status: The guardian of the old temple ruins and the genealogy keeper are both elders concerned with preservation and are often seen in counsel.
payload.bond: Zel guards the stones; Aja guards the names that went with them. Together they are the memory of a people whose written record is sparse, and they spend long evenings matching Aja's oral lineages to the carvings Zel protects. Their shared fear is that when one of them dies, half the memory dies too.

entries.name: Rainforest guide and river-reader expedition guide

payload.public_status: Boca Path-Finder and Sávio River-Reader are both expedition guides and are known to compete for the same outsider contracts.
payload.bond: Boca knows the land; Sávio knows the water. Outsiders hire one or the other, and the two guides resent the lost commissions acutely. Each has deliberately fed the other bad leads at least once, and the frontier community's patience with their feud is wearing thin — though neither will be the first to concede.

payload.public_status: The raid captain and the guard captain are the two foremost women-at-arms of Skaldvik, and their differing views on the settlement's future are well known.
payload.bond: Astrid believes the fjords grow wealthy by raiding; Ingrid believes they grow safe by guarding. Each commands the loyalty of fighters the other needs, and neither will yield authority. The jarl keeps them both because their friction prevents either from growing too powerful — a balance neither woman has failed to notice.

payload.public_status: The seer and the skald are often seen together, the one who sees the future and the one who remembers the past.
payload.bond: Their friendship is the partnership of memory and foresight — Yrsa's visions are incomplete without Eira's knowledge of what has already happened, and Eira's histories feel lifeless without Yrsa's sense of where they are pointing. They finish each other's prophecies, and it unsettles everyone who watches them do it.

payload.public_status: Greta Keelson and Bjorn Keelwright are both shipwrights of Skaldvik, and their competing longships are launched from adjacent slipways.
payload.bond: Bjorn trained Greta, and Greta now builds ships that some say outperform her old master's. Bjorn is proud and stung in equal measure — he cannot decide whether his apprentice surpassing him is his triumph or his defeat. Greta respects him and will not say so, because to her it would sound like pity.

payload.public_status: Brita Whalejaw and Olaf Whaleback are both veteran whalers and are known to drink together after the season's hunt.
payload.bond: They have crewed the same boat for more seasons than either can count, and the bond is the wordless kind forged in shared danger — each has hauled the other out of the black water. Neither speaks of it; in Hrafnland, that is how you say I would die for you.

payload.public_status: Ragna Forgebreak and Sten Ironwake are both smiths serving the Skaldvik community, and their competing work is a common comparison.
payload.bond: They share a forge because neither can afford to build a second, and they have divided the work by a grudging agreement — she forges the tools, he forges the weapons. The arrangement works but chafes; each believes the other's half is the easier one, and the forge rings with pointed silences.

payload.public_status: Hilla Snowstep and Ulf Shadowstep are both hunters and trappers of the fjords and are known to run traplines in the same country.
payload.bond: They met as rivals disputing a valley's pelts and nearly killed each other the first winter. They ended the second winter sharing a fire and a kill, having realized the valley was rich enough for both and the cold was the real enemy. They now coordinate their lines and split the take, a peace neither mentions for fear of jinxing it.

entries.name: Healer and herbalist of the fjords

payload.public_status: The healer and the herbalist are known to work closely together, Siv treating wounds and Dis Lea providing the medicines.
payload.bond: They are the two women between whom most of the fjords' sick pass, and their cooperation is seamless because they long ago stopped arguing over whose skill a case required. Their quiet friendship is a mercy in a place where mercy is scarce, and the community knows it even if the two women never say it of themselves.

payload.public_status: Gerd is the sister of Jarl Sigrid Hallvarsdottir and a farmer of the hall lands, and their kinship is well known.
payload.bond: Gerd chose the plow where Sigrid chose the hall, and each secretly envies the other — Gerd the authority, Sigrid the quiet. They love each other with the particular fierceness of sisters who were once the only family the other had, and they fight with the same intensity, always about how best to protect the people they both refuse to lose.

payload.public_status: Torsten Coinwave and Sigunn Ironbar are the two principal traders of Skaldvik, and their competition for import contracts is open.
payload.bond: Each controls a different trade route — Torsten the southern, Sigunn the northern — and each has been trying to buy into the other's for years. Their rivalry is courteous on the surface and ruthless below it; the moment one stumbles, the other will absorb the route, and both know it.

payload.public_status: Edda Cloudcarver and Erik Frostbeard are both elders of Skaldvik and are known to trade stories at the longfire.
payload.bond: Between them they hold most of the settlement's living memory, and they spend their evenings testing each other's recollections against their own — correcting, supplementing, occasionally discovering they remember the same event entirely differently. The friendship is the settlement's archive, kept warm by two people who know they are its last custodians.

entries.name: Bondservant and the midwife who advocates for her

payload.public_status: Kata Mossheart the midwife is known to look in on Thyra Wildseed, a thrall in service to the hall, and Thyra is known to assist at births.
payload.bond: Kata has been quietly teaching Thyra the midwife's craft — an act of quiet defiance in a place where a thrall is not supposed to learn a respected trade. Thyra is becoming the midwife's hands where Kata's are failing with age. The unspoken plan is that one day Thyra will take over, and the hall will have to decide whether it can afford to lose her labor.

entries.name: Two binding family scions, Idris and al-Sayf

payload.public_status: Malik Idris of the Idris family and Tariq al-Sayf, patriarch of the al-Sayf family, are the two foremost figures of the binding families and their competition for Council influence is public.
payload.bond: Their families have controlled rival contracts for generations, and the two men have inherited a feud older than either of them. Each respects the other's cunning and would never say so, because in Al-Khayzar the admission of an equal is the first step toward being outmaneuvered by one.

entries.name: Idris reformer daughter and al-Faris scholar heiress

payload.public_status: The Idris daughter and the al-Faris heiress are both educated women of the binding families and are known to correspond on scholarly matters.
payload.bond: They are friends across a family rivalry, bound by a shared frustration with the limits their houses place on women. Each is the other's only peer who understands what it is to be brilliant and contained. They have begun to wonder, privately, whether their friendship could become an alliance their families would forbid.

entries.name: The Spice Queen and the political agitator merchant

payload.public_status: Layla the Spice Queen and Yasmin al-Barrani are the two most powerful spice merchants in Al-Khayzar, and their competition is the talk of the market.
payload.bond: Their rivalry is not merely commercial — Layla defends the old Pact and the council order; Yasmin agitates against it, using her trade network to fund reform. Each believes the other's vision would ruin the city, and the spice market is the battlefield where their politics is actually fought.

payload.public_status: The head gardener of the Hanging Gardens and the water finder are known to work together, each enabling the other's craft.
payload.bond: Amira finds the water; Ghada makes it bloom. Their partnership is the quiet engine that keeps the Hanging Gardens alive in a desert city, and the friendship has grown from years of shared, unglamorous labor before dawn. Neither seeks credit; both know the gardens would die without the other.

payload.public_status: The master calligrapher and the court poet are known collaborators, Inas composing verses that Rania renders in fine script.
payload.bond: Their partnership is artistic and personal — each believes the other's craft completes their own, and the collaboration is the deepest relationship in either of their lives, though neither has named it as such. They work in a companionable silence that the court has learned not to interrupt.

entries.name: Two lamp makers, one accidental jailer and one djinn-blooded

payload.public_status: Esam al-Misbah and Nisreen al-Misbah are both lamp makers of the same quarter and are assumed to be kin by their shared craft surname.
payload.bond: They are cousins, and each holds a secret the other does not know: Esam accidentally imprisoned a djinn in a lamp and cannot release it; Nisreen carries hidden djinn blood. The irony — a jailer of djinn and a daughter of djinn in the same family — is a tension waiting to break, because neither has told the other and their crafts are converging.

payload.public_status: The caravan guard captain and the falconer work the same desert routes and are known to coordinate on caravan security, her birds scouting the road.
payload.bond: Their friendship is the trust of people who guard each other's lives across open desert, where a wrong turn means death. What Karim does not know is that Muna's birds also detect djinn — and she has been quietly steering his caravans away from places where the djinn-touched walk, protecting him from something he does not believe in.

payload.public_status: A beggar and a courier of Al-Khayzar are not publicly known to have any relationship.
payload.bond: Isam runs a shadow intelligence network from the gutter, and Bushra is his fastest courier — together they move information that the binding families would kill to suppress. Isam was once a scribe and Bushra knows it; she is the only person who still addresses him by his old name, and he has never decided whether that is mercy or a threat.

entries.name: Al-Sayf heir and the djinn-confidante daughter

payload.public_status: The al-Sayf heir and Zahra al-Dhahab, a daughter of another binding family, are publicly acquainted through binding family circles.
payload.bond: They are secretly in love across a family rivalry, and Zahra's djinn-confidante is the only being that knows — she confided in the spirit because she had no human she trusted. The djinn, bound to her family, has its own opinions about the match, and Zahra is no longer certain whether her confidante is keeping her secret or engineering something with it.

entries.name: Physician and herbalist, mentor and student

payload.public_status: Afaf al-A'shab the herbalist is known to supply Shifa al-Tabib the physician with rare medicinal plants, and the two consult on difficult cases.
payload.bond: Shifa is teaching Afaf the djinn-fire medicine that no herbalist is supposed to learn, because she has realized Afaf's contract-bearing status makes her one of the few who can safely handle it. The teaching is covert and accelerates a trust neither expected; Afaf is beginning to suspect Shifa is grooming a successor for something she has not yet explained.

payload.public_status: The snake charmer and the porter are both minor figures of the same quarter and are known to share a water pipe at day's end.
payload.bond: Both are touched by the djinn in ways no one else can see — Hassan charms them as he charms serpents, and Omar sees them where others see nothing. They are the only two people in each other's lives who understand what it is to walk through a city full of invisible presences, and their friendship is the relief of no longer being alone with it.

payload.public_status: Kai is a wayfinder of the guilds and Hoku Star-Path is a veteran navigator; Kai is known to have trained in part under Hoku's guidance.
payload.bond: Hoku sees in Kai the navigator who will one day surpass him, and is teaching him everything he knows precisely because he wants to be surpassed — the old wayfinder's grief is that his own star-reading is fading with his eyes. Kai resists the implication that Hoku is preparing to retire, because accepting it means accepting the weight of being the best.

payload.public_status: Tamatoa is the son of Chief Lani and a fisher of the atoll, and his position as the chief's son is well known.
payload.bond: Lani is preparing Tamatoa to lead but worries he is too gentle for it — he fishes because he loves the sea, not because he wants to govern it. Tamatoa dreads the day his mother steps down and the responsibility falls to him, but would never shame her by saying so. Each is trying to protect the other from the truth about the future.

entries.name: Elder wayfinder and chant keeper elder

payload.public_status: Elder Wayfinder Pua and Vehina the Rememberer are both elders of the archipelago and are known to be close, the keeper of the star paths and the keeper of the chants.
payload.bond: Between them they hold the two halves of navigation — Pua the stars, Vehina the songs that encode the routes. Their friendship is the partnership of two women whose knowledge, combined, is the only complete map of the archipelago, and who know that when one dies the other will be the last living chart.

payload.public_status: Mana the Tattoo-carver is known to mark the routes on the bodies of navigators, and Fetu Star-Reader, a junior wayfinder, is among those she has carved.
payload.bond: The tattoos Mana carves encode the star paths in a language only wayfinders read, and she has begun teaching Fetu not just to receive them but to carve them himself — a craft usually kept from navigators. The reason is private: her hands are stiffening with age, and she needs someone who can both navigate and inscribe to carry the routes forward.

payload.public_status: Tama Pearl-Blood is a pearl diver apprentice under Hina Deepwater, and the two are known to dive together.
payload.bond: Hina is pushing Tama to dive deeper than is safe because the best pearls are deeper, and Tama is pushing back — the apprentice is starting to suspect the master's ambition is not for the pearls but for the legend of being the deepest diver who ever lived. The friendship is fraying into a test of wills that the sea will arbitrate.

payload.public_status: Leilani Wave-Singer, a sail maker of the wayfinder guilds, has taken on Rotama Quiet-Weave as her apprentice.
payload.bond: Rotama has a gift for reading the weave that Leilani has not seen in a generation — the apprentice can feel where a sail will catch before it is raised. Leilani is teaching her everything and holding nothing back, because she has recognized that her student will exceed her and wants nothing more than to see it.

entries.name: Refugee former chief and community organizer

payload.public_status: Ariki Lost-Chief, a refugee and former chief, and Vanya Salt-Home, a refugee community organizer, are known to lead the refugee council together.
payload.bond: Ariki lost his atoll and his authority with it, and Vanya has become the voice of the displaced because she can speak to the host communities in a way a deposed chief cannot. Their partnership is the leadership of a people with no land, and it rests on a shared refusal to let their community dissolve into the archipelago's margins.

entries.name: Canoe builder and refugee canoe builder

payload.public_status: Tane Hull-Shaper, a canoe builder of the guilds, and Solomona Drowned-Home, a refugee canoe builder, work the same waterfront and are known to share tools.
payload.bond: Solomona lost his workshop when his atoll drowned; Tane opened his. The friendship is the quiet generosity of one craftsman to another, and it has become something more — Tane is learning the hull designs of Solomona's lost people, preserving them in wood so they are not lost to the sea that took the rest.

entries.name: Shell carver and bone carver, rival artists

payload.public_status: Rina Shell-Carver and Pili Bone-Cutter are both carvers of the archipelago — she of shell, he of bone — and their competing artistry is a common comparison.
payload.bond: They are the two finest carvers of the archipelago, working in different materials, and each believes their medium is the truer one. The rivalry is artistic but bitter, because both were trained by the same master who chose neither as successor, and each has spent the years since trying to prove the dead master wrong.

payload.public_status: The kava brewer and the cook are known to collaborate on feast preparations and are often seen at the same work fires.
payload.bond: Their friendship is the easy warmth of two women whose crafts complete a gathering — Mere feeds the body, Pilialoha settles the spirit. They have been friends since girlhood, and the kava brew is as much Mere's recipe as Pilialoha's, though only one of them is named for it.

payload.public_status: Koa Far-Eye and Tala Quiet-Foot are both scouts — he of the wayfinder guilds, she of the same — and their competing methods are a running debate.
payload.bond: Koa scouts from the high points with his eyes; Tala scouts on foot through the brush. Each believes their method superior and each is right about different things, which is why the wayfinder guilds employ both. The rivalry is a competition for the single senior scout position that will open when the current holder retires, and both want it.

payload.public_status: The feather worker and the wood carver of the wayfinder guilds are known to collaborate on ceremonial regalia — she providing the feathers, he the carved bases.
payload.bond: Their crafts interlock — his carved wood holds her featherwork — and the collaboration has grown into a friendship built on shared perfectionism. Each is the only other person who understands how long the other spends on a detail no one else will notice, and that recognition is its own kind of intimacy.

_help: The engine of the campaign. A thread is something unresolved that will
get worse if ignored.
`next_possible_moves` is the most valuable field in this file. Write the
two or three things that could happen NEXT if the player does nothing.
It is what stops a scene ending on a still frame, and you should revise
it as the campaign moves.
`pressure` here IS live. `stakes` is what is lost if it resolves badly.

payload.summary: A soul new to Gaia has arrived in the Heavenly Realm. The Guide is waiting to help them choose a nation to begin in. The choice is real and permanent — once they walk down into one of the seven nations, they cannot come back to choose again.
payload.stakes: The player's starting nation determines which conflicts they land in the middle of, which people they meet first, and what kind of life they begin. A wrong choice is not death — it is a different story.
next_possible_moves: The Guide describes each of the seven nations in a sentence or two and asks where the player wants to begin.
If the player hesitates, the Guide offers to describe one in more detail — but only one.
If the player asks too many questions, the Guide gently reminds them that the choice is meant to be partly blind.

payload.summary: In Valdris, no new dragon bond has been made in twenty years. The dragon-bonded knights are fracturing between reformers and traditionalists. The king is aging and the succession is unspoken. Sir Aldrich's own dragon, Verath, has gone silent — a secret he keeps because admitting it would confirm the order's worst fears.
payload.stakes: If the order fractures completely, Valdris loses its most powerful defenders. If the succession crisis hits while the order is broken, the kingdom could face civil war. Aldrich's secret, if exposed, accelerates both.
next_possible_moves: The reformist faction calls a formal vote to dissolve the traditional oath requirements, which the traditionalists have promised to refuse — publicly and loudly.
Sir Aldrich's dragon Verath descends from the mountain roosts for the first time in three years and lands in the Dragonrest courtyard, silent, refusing to speak to anyone — including Aldrich.
The king's eldest son visits Dragonrest to 'inspect the order,' a move the traditionalists see as a threat and the reformers see as an opportunity.

payload.summary: The three-year truce between Jin, Chu, and Wei is nearing its end. One border skirmish has already happened between Jin and Wei forces at the Long Pass. The younger officers at the Great Academy in Jin'an speak openly about ending the truce. Warlord Cao Shen is dying faster than anyone knows and wants reunification before he goes.
payload.stakes: If the truce breaks, the largest war in a generation begins. The last war killed tens of thousands. Sangguo's trade routes feed half of Gaia — a war disrupts everything, everywhere.
next_possible_moves: A second skirmish at the Long Pass — this time with casualties on both sides, each blaming the other.
Cao Shen's court physician is found dead in the palace, an apparent suicide that the warlord's spymaster does not believe was suicide.
Chu's warlord Sun Liang receives a secret envoy from Wei proposing an alliance against Jin — and the envoy is intercepted by Jin scouts.

payload.summary: In the Tide Archipelago, sea levels are rising. Islands are losing their shores. The voyagers are being pushed inward toward crowded volcanic islands. Wayfinder Kai has lost three routes this year and the sea spirits have gone silent when asked about the cause. In Verdania, Shaman Nara's river spirit has sent a warning it does not fully understand — and the two problems may be connected.
payload.stakes: If the rising continues, the Tide Archipelago loses its civilization within a generation. If the cause is something that can be stopped, every month of delay costs islands. If it cannot be stopped, the voyagers become refugees in nations that do not want them.
next_possible_moves: Two more outer islets submerge during a storm, displacing forty families who arrive at Lani Atoll with nothing.
Kai attempts a solo voyage to the deepest water in the Archipelago to sing to the sea spirits directly — and they answer, but not in words he recognizes.
Shaman Nara's river spirit delivers a fragment of a warning that mentions 'the deep place' and 'the old door,' phrases it has never used before.

payload.summary: In Al-Khayzar, Malik Idris is the firstborn of his generation — and his family's oldest djinn contract demands the firstborn of each generation as payment. The djinn Zuhayr has begun appearing to Malik, patient and polite, reminding him that the contract is almost due. Malik has searched secretly for a way out and found nothing.
payload.stakes: If Malik cannot break or renegotiate the contract, he is taken by the djinn — not killed, but bound to Zuhayr's service for the rest of his natural life. If he breaks the contract wrongly, the Pact of the Lamp may fracture, and the peace between Al-Khayzar's city-states dies with it.
next_possible_moves: Zuhayr appears to Malik in the Star Bazaar, visible to other binders for the first time, making the debt publicly known — which Malik's family will treat as a deliberate humiliation.
Malik's younger sister discovers his research notes and confronts him — she is not bound by the contract, but she has her own reasons for wanting the family's debts exposed.
A stranger arrives in Zaffar claiming to know a method of contract renegotiation that does not violate the Pact — and asking a price that may be worse than the djinn's.

payload.summary: In Tsukuyomi, the shrine network that keeps wild yokai at a distance from settled areas is weakening. Rural shrines are being neglected as the central authority funnels resources to the capital. Miko Sora maintains her shrine alone, but the ward she tends is one of a chain, and links upstream of her are failing. If enough links break, the yokai pressure on the Cedar Road becomes dangerous.
payload.stakes: If the ward chain breaks along the Cedar Road, the pilgrimage route becomes unsafe and the mountain villages lose their protection. Wild yokai are not monsters — they are unpredictable, and people die when the boundary is weak.
next_possible_moves: Sora notices the upstream shrine's ward has gone dark — the keeper there has left, and no replacement was sent.
A farmer from the next valley arrives in Haru's Shrine Town reporting yokai sightings on the Cedar Road — something that has not happened in a generation.
A messenger from the Great Shrine in Tsuki-no-Miyako arrives with an order: Sora is to report to the capital for reassignment. Her shrine will be 'temporarily' unstaffed.

payload.summary: In Hrafnland, Jarl Sigrid believes the frost giants of the deep mountains are preparing to expand southward. She has been quietly building a coalition of jarls who want to push the giants back. The Althing will not authorize action without proof, and proof requires scouting territory no scout has returned from. Her coalition is not as unified as she presents it.
payload.stakes: If Sigrid acts without Althing approval, she splits Hrafnland and may trigger a jarls' war. If she does nothing and the giants are expanding, the northern fjords are overrun. If she is wrong about the giants' intentions, she has spent political capital on a phantom threat.
next_possible_moves: A trader from a northern fjord arrives in Skaldvik with a story: a fishing village was found abandoned, the boats still at the dock, no sign of violence — and no sign of the people.
One of Sigrid's coalition jarls privately withdraws his support, telling her the Althing will see her coalition as a power grab, not a defense.
A scout Sigrid sent into the deep mountains returns — the first to return — and will not speak about what he saw. He has gone white-haired and will not leave the mead hall.

payload.summary: Kuro the Smoke, a cat-folk thief in Tsuki-no-Miyako, stole a document from a daimyo's estate that contains evidence of Takeda's coalition plans. He does not understand what he has, but Takeda's agents are hunting him. The document's trail leads through the underworld of Tsukuyomi and potentially to Sangguo's information broker Zhou Ba, who would sell it to the highest bidder.
payload.stakes: If Takeda's agents recover the document, Kuro is dead and the coalition remains secret. If Zhou Ba sells it to Cao Shen, Sangguo gains leverage over Tsukuyomi's internal politics. If it goes public, the shogunate cracks down on the provincial clans and the coalition goes underground or open revolt.
next_possible_moves: Takeda's agents trace Kuro to the merchant district and close the gates, starting a block-by-block search.
Kuro contacts a middleman to reach Zhou Ba in Sangguo, not knowing that the middleman is also working for Takeda.
Shogun Ashikara's spymaster independently learns that a document was stolen from a daimyo's estate and begins his own investigation — the shogun wants to know what Takeda is hiding.

payload.summary: King Aldran is dying and has not named an heir. Princess Elara backs the reformist faction and secret dragonbone research. Prince Roderick commands the military and is secretly courting the bandit lord Garrick as a deniable asset. The youngest, Tomas, is unaligned. The court is a cold war of positioning, and the king is running out of time.
payload.stakes: If the king dies without naming an heir, civil war. If Roderick wins, the old order hardens and the reformists are purged. If Elara wins, the dragon order is reformed and the old nobility loses power. If Tomas wins — no one knows, including Tomas.
next_possible_moves: The king's physician quietly informs the court that the king's condition is worsening — the information leaks within a day.
Roderick makes Garrick a formal offer: pardon and a commission in exchange for blocking the Greywood road against Elara's merchant allies.
Elara's reformist researchers achieve a partial resonance from a dragonbone artifact — the first proof that an artificial bond might be possible — and someone in her team talks.

payload.summary: Garrick the Wolf controls a stretch of the Greywood road in Valdris. He is being courted by Prince Roderick as a deniable asset. Maggie Pippin at the Copper Kettle has noticed increased armed traffic. The crown's patrols are getting more aggressive. Garrick's men are hungry and loyal, but loyalty has a shelf life.
payload.stakes: If Garrick accepts Roderick's offer, Roderick gains a deniable military asset on the main trade road. If the crown catches Garrick first, his men scatter and the road becomes truly lawless. If Garrick finds another path — a pardon from the king directly, or a war that needs soldiers — the equation changes entirely.
next_possible_moves: A crown patrol ambushes one of Garrick's foraging parties, killing two men — the first blood on the road this season, and it demands a response.
Roderick sends a sealed letter through Maggie's inn offering terms: full pardon, a captain's commission, and control of the road in exchange for blocking Elara's merchant traffic.
Garrick's second-in-command, a woman named Brita, challenges his leadership at a campfire meeting — she wants to accept Roderick's offer and argues that waiting is dying.

payload.summary: Wen Li, the river-folk canal master in Jin'an, has been warning that the canal system feeding the city's grain supply is failing. Two years of ignored reports and diverted maintenance funds have brought the system to the edge. Wen Li is considering sabotage to force the court's attention.
payload.stakes: If the canals fail, Jin'an loses its grain supply within a season. Two hundred thousand people face famine. If Wen Li sabotages a canal to prove her point, the shortage is immediate but the political will to repair is forced. Either way, people suffer.
next_possible_moves: A canal gate fails during a moderate rain, flooding a market district — a preview of what a full failure looks like, and a warning Wen Li did not engineer.
Wen Li's written report is finally read by Strategist Mei Lin, who realizes the canal crisis connects to the truce: military spending has been eating infrastructure budgets for three years.
General Lu Fang orders the canal workers conscripted into military labor, arguing that fortifying the Long Pass is more urgent than canal maintenance. Wen Li is not consulted.

payload.summary: Kaa the Jaguar-kin found a temple door in the deep jungle of Verdania that was not open before and is warm to the touch. Dr. Voss has calculated a convergence point in the same area. Shaman Nara's river spirit has warned of 'the deep place' and 'the old door.' Monk Jian Yi is walking south toward the same location. Volva Helga has seen it in visions. Multiple independent sources are converging on the same point.
payload.stakes: If the door is opening on its own, something is changing beneath the world. If multiple people are being drawn to it independently, the door may be calling them — or whatever is behind the door is. What is behind it is unknown, but everything touching it — river spirits, sea spirits, whales, chi monks, volva, and shamans — is frightened.
next_possible_moves: Kaa goes back to the door alone, drunk and armed, and this time it is open — warm air pouring out of it, carrying a smell like deep water and old stone.

Jian Yi arrives at the Mist Falls trading post on the edge of Verdania, the first leg of his journey complete, and asks a trader about the temple cities — the trader is Amara, Kaa's cousin, who connects him to Iara.
Shaman Nara's river spirit delivers a new warning: the door is not opening because something is pushing from outside. Something is pushing from inside.

payload.summary: Fatima Idris has discovered her brother Malik's research into breaking the family's djinn contract. She wants to use his crisis to expose the binding families' unsustainable contract system and force reform. She has not told Malik what she knows. Judge Tariq is independently worried about the oldest contracts destabilizing. Layla the Spice Queen is watching, ready to pick up the pieces.
payload.stakes: If Fatima exposes the contracts publicly, the binding families lose face and the council fractures — reform or chaos. If Malik breaks his contract badly, the Pact of the Lamp may fail and the city-states' peace dies. If Judge Tariq finds a legal remedy, there is a path through the law — but the law may not have one.
next_possible_moves: Fatima anonymously leaks a summary of the Idris family's oldest contract to a merchant in the Star Bazaar — not the full text, but enough to start rumors.
Judge Tariq summons Malik to his court, not as a defendant but as a consultant — he wants to understand the Idris contract's structure because it is the oldest and may be the first to break.
Zuhayr appears to Malik in public, at the Star Bazaar, visible to other binders — making the debt common knowledge and forcing the family to acknowledge it.

payload.summary: Rashid the Sand-walker has found a working fragment of the Old Road in the deep desert of Al-Khayzar — a two-hour stretch connecting the Mirror Oasis to a point near the Verdania border. The fragment hums like a voice, which is not how Old Roads behave. He is deciding who to tell, and the hum is getting louder.
payload.stakes: A working Old Road fragment is the most valuable secret in Gaia — it could connect Al-Khayzar to Verdania in hours instead of months. If the hum is a voice, the Road may be doing something Old Roads are not supposed to do. If the wrong person learns about it, the secret becomes a weapon.
next_possible_moves: Rashid returns to the fragment to find that the hum has changed — it is now a rhythm, almost a heartbeat, and the air above the Road is shimmering.
A binding family agent notices Rashid's absences and follows him to the Mirror Oasis, not to the fragment itself but close enough to suspect something.
The fragment extends — the Road is growing, clearing itself, pushing back the sand, and the hum is now audible from the oasis.

payload.summary: Fin the Whale-speaker has learned that the great whales are leaving the Tide Archipelago — not migrating, but departing permanently. They are swimming south, past Verdania, toward the open ocean. The images they send him — deep water, a door, something waking — match the warnings from Shaman Nara, Monk Jian Yi, and Volva Helga. Without the whales, voyaging in the Archipelago becomes vastly more dangerous.
payload.stakes: If the whales leave, the Archipelago loses its oldest allies and voyaging becomes far more dangerous. The displaced islanders cannot be relocated if the sea routes are unsafe. Whatever is driving the whales south is connected to the same force that is opening doors and frightening spirits across the world.
next_possible_moves: The last family of whales in the northern Archipelago sends a final image to Fin — a clear picture of the door, from the other side, showing something behind it that is large and moving — then the whales turn south and are gone.
Kai's attempt to sing to the sea spirits at the deepest water goes wrong: the spirits answer, but not in words he recognizes, and the current around his boat changes direction against the wind.
Elder Wayfinder Pua announces to the guild that she will sing the deepest song — the one she has not sung in forty years — and the guild argues about whether it is safe.

payload.summary: Daimyo Takeda Renji is building a coalition of rural clans who feel the shogunate has abandoned them. He has a secret alliance with the wild kitsune Tamamo, who is willing to create yokai incidents to prove the shrine network's weakness. His plans were stolen by the thief Kuro, and the document is now in play. The shogun is dying and the succession is undecided.
payload.stakes: If Takeda's coalition succeeds in forcing the shogunate's hand, the provinces gain power and the shrine network is repaired — but Takeda is positioned as kingmaker. If the coalition is exposed prematurely, it becomes a rebellion. If Tamamo engineers a yokai incident that kills people, Takeda's legitimate grievance becomes a bloody opportunism.
next_possible_moves: Tamamo engineers a yokai breach on the Cedar Road — nothing fatal, but enough to frighten pilgrims and prove the wards are weak. Takeda uses the incident at the next clan council to argue that the shogunate has failed.
The shogun's spymaster traces the stolen document to Takeda's estate and begins investigating the daimyo's coalition — quietly, because accusing a daimyo without proof is a political act.

The shogun's elder son, Ashikara Kenji, confronts Takeda at court — not about the coalition, which he does not know about, but about the yokai incident, which he blames on Takeda's territory being poorly defended. The irony is not lost on Takeda.

payload.summary: Mana the Tattoo-carver believes that wayfinder tattoos are not just records — they are anchors. When a route is submerged and the tattoo fades, the wayfinder feels it as physical pain.
